§ 62 — SheHechiyanu [Who Has Kept Us Alive]: Time Derives from the Obstructer; Joy Gives Life to Time

SheHechiyanu v'kiy'manu v'higi'anu laz'man hazeh [Who has kept us alive, sustained us, and brought us to this time] — blessed over every joy that comes from time to time. The essential Birchas SheHechiyanu [the Blessing of Who Has Kept Us Alive] is on the Yamim Tovim. The essential formation of time derives at its root from the aspect of the waiting until it settles, as above. In truth there is no time at all (as explained on "I have this day begotten you," LM II:61). All of time exists only for the sake of free will — man must pass through this world for the span of his allotted days in order to bind time to that which is above time. This world is in place and time; man must pass through it to bind the aspects of time and place to that which is above time (see Hilchos Milah 4 on the above Torah).

The essential time derives from the above waiting — the Arranger and Settler of the mind (= the obstructer). The essential tikun is through the joy of the mitzvah, through mi yaimar. Man comes to this world only for this: to know Hashem through the perception of the above nine chambers, through which the Ain Sof light is perceived in mati v'lo mati. All this is impossible except through the Arranger and Settler — the aspect of waiting until it settles. All the days of man's life are only in the aspect of waiting — so he may settle properly in true yishuv hada'as, through which he will perceive what he perceives according to his true service — what even the angels do not merit perceiving. For the angels cannot perceive His Ain Sof light in this manner like man can, because they did not properly rectify the Arranger and Settler — which is only rectified through the power of free will that only man possesses (see Hilchos Nefilas Apayim on the Torah "Amtza'isa"). They burn and clamor to perceive Him, and though their perception is very lofty, it has no comparison to the perception of the righteous man who was in this world and withstood his trials through free will — thereby meriting rectifying the mind. The essential tikun is rectifying the Arranger and Settler (= the waiting), from which all time derives. All of man's time — all the days of his life — are the aspect of waiting: he is told to wait the time of his life, to settle himself each day and each moment. Through this he will merit perceiving at each moment what he perceives, until on his final day he ascends with all the days and time he spent in this world — ascending to where he ascends, perceiving the lights of the tzachtzachos that the tzadikim merit: "He shall satisfy your soul with tzachtzachos" — fortunate are they.

The essential thing is merited through performing mitzvos with joy. Joy is the vitality and sustenance of all man's days — for in truth there is no time at all. As we see even physically: they are nothing, for time flies exceedingly — a passing shadow, drifting dust, a fading cloud, etc. The past is gone, the future not yet here, and the present is but an eye-blink (as brought in many sefarim). "The days of our lives are vanity, vanity of vanities" (Midrash Koheles, Parshah 1) — like the vapor of the seventh vessel, having no substance. Nothing remains of all past, present, and future time except what one snatches from it: some good — Torah, tefilah, tzedakah, good deeds, intense desire and longing for Hashem, closeness to tzadikim and true friends, etc. The essential thing is joy — the point of all mitzvos, the essential vitality and sustenance.

Therefore the essential vitality (in time and place) is through the day and time one merits the joy of the mitzvah — rejoicing in Him: "this is the day Hashem has made — let us exult and rejoice in it." Only "this is the day Hashem has made" — when one merits exulting and rejoicing in it. From there comes all vitality and sustenance of the days and times (= the days of man's life). The wicked, who do not merit the joy of the mitzvah, truly have no vitality — therefore our Sages say: "the wicked in their lifetimes are called dead," since they do not merit binding time to that which is above time, receiving vitality from the Source of Life through the joy of the mitzvah. Conversely, even the great tzadikim, if they do not take care to wait until they settle properly and their minds pursue excessively — they cannot live in this world at all: "when they drew near before Hashem and died"; "he peeked and died."

Therefore the essential vitality of the days and times man lives in this world is through the above — meriting the tikun of the Settler and Arranger properly through performing mitzvos with joy. Then he merits coming and ascending with all his days and times to where he ascends: "Avraham was old, coming with his days" — "he was old and entered with his days," as the holy Zohar states. Therefore at every time of joy we bless: SheHechiyanu v'kiy'manu v'higi'anu laz'man hazeh [Who has kept us alive, sustained us, and brought us to this time] — the essential vitality and sustenance of all our days is through reaching this time of joy: "this is the day Hashem has made." These are the sanctified times of the Yamim Tovim, where His G-dliness is revealed through the great miracles and wonders He performed (= the essential joy), or when one sees a friend and rejoices (= the joy of the mitzvah).

§ 63 — SheHechiyanu [Who Has Kept Us Alive] on a New Fruit: All Growth Derives from the Joy of Mitzvos

Even on a new fruit we bless SheHechiyanu [Who Has Kept Us Alive], as our Sages say: "I also say the blessing of z'man on a new pumpkin." All the growing and sprouting of fruits is through the joy of mitzvos that sustains the entire world (created for the Torah's sake). As explained in the Torah "Arichas Apayim" (LM I:155): all the power of growth and sprouting is through emunah (= joy). As it says: "the meadows are clothed with flocks, the valleys covered with grain — they shout for joy, they also sing." And in many verses the great joy through the sprouting of fruits is explained: "the blossoms have appeared in the land, the time of singing has arrived." All the growing and sprouting of fruits each year is through the point of mitzvos (= joy in Him). Fruits and grain sustain every living soul — essentially man, whose essential vitality is the holy da'as to know Him — through performing mitzvos with joy. Therefore we bless SheHechiyanu [Who Has Kept Us Alive] over them.

§ 64 — The Thirty-Day Interval: Repairing the Moon's Blemish

Therefore the essential birchas haz'man [blessing of time] requires seeing the thing after at least thirty days — for continuous pleasure is no pleasure (as is known). The essential vitality is through the above waiting — the root of joy. The measure is thirty days (= a month), corresponding to the filling of the moon's blemish. Then is the essential tikun of joy — repairing "luminaries" (deficient), from which all sadness derives (as in ois lamed above) — transforming it to joy.

segments.he: וזה בחינת תפלת ערבית רשות. כי יעקב תקן תפלת ערבית . כי התפלה היא בחינת חדוש העולם כמבאר ומובן בדברי רבנו זכרונו לברכה בכמה מקומות . כי התפלה היא אחדותו יתברך בבחינת הוא תהלתך והוא אלקיך . והדבור של התפלה הוא בחינת דבר ה' שעל ידו נעשו שמים וארץ. בבחינת בדבר ה' שמים נעשו, כמבאר בדברי רבנו זכרונו לברכה במקום אחר . וזה בחינת אד' שפתי תפתח שאומרים קדם התפלה, כי הדבור של התפלה הוא דבר ה' כנזכר לעיל. נמצא שהתפלה היא בחינת חדוש העולם בחינת דבר ה' וכו' כנ"ל. ועל כן תפלת ערבית רשות. כי התגלות הבריאה הוא בחינת אור בחינת ויאמר אלקים יהי אור וכו' . וקדם הבריאה זה בחינת חשך. כי קדם הבריאה אי אפשר להשיג, ועל כן נקרא בחינת חשך מעמק המשג. בבחינת יוצר אור ובורא חשך. כמו שאיתא בכונות , שיצירה נקרא אור ובריאה חשך, מחמת שבריאה למעלה מיצירה ואי אפשר להשיג שם, על כן נקרא חשך מעמק המשג. בחינת ישת חשך סתרו . ועל כן גם בשעת הבריאה ברא ה' יתברך החשך קדם להאור ברישא חשוכא והדר נהורא. כי החשך שקדם להאור מרמז על קדם הבריאה שהוא בחינת ישת חשך סתרו. ואז בבחינת חשך בבחינת קדם הבריאה דהינו קדם שנאצלו נשמות ישראל, אז היה העולם בחינת אפשרי המציאות מאחר שעדין לא נבראו נשמות ישראל וכנזכר לעיל. וזה בחינת תפלת ערבית רשות. כי התפלה היא בחינת בריאת העולם. כי התפלה יש לה שרש למעלה, כי גם ה' יתברך מתפלל כמו שאמרו רבותינו זכרונם לברכה מנין שהקדוש ברוך הוא מתפלל וכו'. ואז בערבית אז התפלה היא בחינת רשות בחינת אפשרי המציאות, כי עדין אין חובה חס ושלום לברא את העולם מאחר שגם נשמות ישראל עדין לא נבראו. ועל כן יעקב תקן תפלת ערבית. כי ישראל עלה במחשבה תחלה כמו שכתוב בראשית ברא וכו' בשביל ישראל שנקראו ראשית וכו'. נמצא שראשית המחשבה של הבריאה היה ישראל, ואז בבחינת ראשית המחשבה היה העולם אפשרי המציאות כנזכר לעיל, מאחר שעדין לא נבראו נשמות ישראל רק שעלה במחשבה, והיה הדבר ברצונו יתברך. ועל כן אז בתחלת הבריאה דהינו כשעלה ישראל במחשבה תחלה אז היה העולם אפשרי המציאות כנזכר לעיל:

§ 65 — Past, Present, and Future: The Threefold Holiness of Time Through Joy

One must revive and gladden his soul through Hashem's kindnesses and goodness — what He did for us in the past, what He does in the present, and what He will do in the future: "He was good, He is good, He will be good to us." This is all the vitality and sustenance of time (= the days of man's life), whose essential thing is to bind them to that which is above time. Each person must search and seek to find within himself good points from the mitzvos he merited performing each day from his youth. For we already merited receiving the Torah and mitzvos through Moshe Rabbainu, which are our life and the length of our days (as explained extensively, especially on "I shall sing to my G-d while I yet live"). Even now, however things are, he snatches some mitzvos every single day — "even the sinners of Israel are full of mitzvos as a pomegranate." The essential thing: to rejoice in this and know the truth — there is no vitality in the world besides this.

The essential thing is what we hope for and anticipate — a good end, through the power of the true tzadikim, as all the prophets and true tzadikim (first and last) have strengthened us. "All Israel has a portion in the World to Come." Even if he is as he is — as long as he believes there is no vitality except Torah and mitzvos, strives and yearns for the eternal purpose, draws close to true tzadikim and friends, and strengthens himself to gladden his soul with the mitzvah-points — he will certainly merit a good end.

Therefore holiness is tripled in all aspects: "Holy, holy, holy"; "the threefold light in threefold time." The essential holiness is joy — through three aspects that are the totality of time: past, present, and future. Their entire vitality and holiness is the joy of the mitzvah — through which time is bound to that which is above time, the very purpose for which man comes to the world.

§ 66 — Shlomo HaMelech in Koheles: The Joy of the Mitzvah Is the Only True Good

This is why Shlomo HaMelech warned greatly in his book Koheles about the joy of the mitzvah: "there is nothing better for a man than to eat and drink and be glad" — our Sages explain: eating and drinking of Torah and mitzvos, and rejoicing on Shabbosos and Yamim Tovim. This is the essential thing. Shlomo speaks at great length in Koheles about the world's vanity, repeating many times the great futility — so man does not deceive himself. Therefore he says: the essential tikun is the joy of the mitzvah — "there is nothing better for man," etc.

He also says: "also every man to whom G-d has given... and to rejoice in his labor" (Koheles 5). "For he shall not much remember the days of his life, because G-d answers him with the joy of his heart" — Rashi explains: Hashem testifies about the joy of his heart — that he rejoiced to do good. This adjoins "he shall not much remember the days of his life": the verse strongly urges man to strengthen himself in joy all the days of his life. Since his days are few and fly exceedingly ("not much") and Koheles speaks extensively of the world's vanity — therefore: "he shall not much" — his days are very few. Let him remember the days of his life — meaning: let him remember to vivify them with true life and sustenance worthy of being called "the days of his life." This is through holy joy — all the vitality. "G-d answers him with the joy of his heart" — Hashem testifies about his heart's joy that he rejoiced to do good. He settled his mind in this world and knew the truth: there is no true vitality except Torah and mitzvos — "for they are our life" — therefore his heart was glad to do good. This is the entire purpose and true sustenance of all the days of his life.

§ 67 — Settling the Mind: The Counsel of Joy Against All Sadness

The principle: man must settle his mind very well at all times — what is he doing in this passing world? What will be his end? What is the purpose of all worldly pursuits and desires? (as explained in LM II:10). The essential obstacle is sadness — every person is full of sadness, worries, sorrow, and sighing: from livelihood, from the great pain of children, etc. — especially from the multitude of sins: "woe is me from my yaitzer; woe is me from my Maker." Although the mussar books say that sadness over sins is good — the ba'al davar and the Chambers of Exchange overpower through such sadness until one is distanced from Hashem even more. The worry over sins would be good if one returned in teshuvah through it — casting away all worldly pursuits and returning completely to Hashem. But the majority of people, especially in these generations, are distanced even more through excessive sadness (even over sins). The Chambers of Exchange reverse the truth and confuse the mind, implanting, chas v'shalom, despair in the heart — as if there is no more hope to renew his days like the eagle. They strengthen the sadness of livelihood ("in sadness you shall eat it") — the craving for wealth, to conduct one's household extravagantly with fine dwellings, household vessels, silver and gold and jewelry — all far beyond one's means. Whatever Hashem provides is never enough: "the more possessions, the more worry." Especially those whose livelihood is pressed, etc. There are many differences among people, but most are filled with sadness, worries, and sorrows without limit — and this is the greatest damage, for through it one cannot settle his mind as to what he is doing in this world.

Therefore one must strengthen himself exceedingly to gladden his soul through all the counsel and ways Rabbainu zichrono livrachah revealed (as explained in the holy sefarim and in our writings extensively). One must remind himself at all times of all the kindnesses, goodnesses, and wonders Hashem has already done for us — collectively and individually: "bless Hashem, my soul, and do not forget all His bounties."

This is the mitzvah of remembering the Exodus from Egypt every day: "so that you remember the day you left Egypt all the days of your life"; "remember this day when you left Egypt." For this all the holy festivals were established — to rejoice in them: "you shall rejoice on your festival" — all remembering the Exodus. One must take to heart and remind himself well of all the kindnesses and wonders of the Exodus and the giving of the Torah, through which we have eternal hope (each and every one of us). "In every generation, a person must see himself as if he himself left Egypt" — for certainly it was not for nothing that He bestowed such kindness with such miracles and wonders, taking us out of Egypt, giving us the Torah, and drawing us close to the true tzadikim in every generation. This kindness will certainly endure forever — "the word of our G-d shall stand forever." And even now He performs miracles daily — what we merit snatching each day: many mitzvos — tzitzis, tefillin, Krias Shma, tefilah, Torah study, etc. We trust, wait, and anticipate salvation at all times — in the end it will surely come, it will not delay: "there is hope for your future."

§ 68 — "Why Do You Leap, O Mountains?": The Foundation of Holiness Can Never Be Destroyed
segments.he_nikud: וְזֶה בְּחִינַת תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית רְשׁוּת. כִּי יַעֲקֹב תִּקֵּן תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית. כִּי הַתְּפִלָּה הִיא בְּחִינַת חִדּוּשׁ הָעוֹלָם כַּמְבֹאָר וּמוּבָן בְּדִבְרֵי רַבֵּנוּ זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה בְּכַמָּה מְקוֹמוֹת. כִּי הַתְּפִלָּה הִיא אַחְדוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בִּבְחִינַת הוּא תְהִלָתֶךָ וְהוּא אֱלֹקֶיךָ. וְהַדִּבּוּר שֶׁל הַתְּפִלָּה הוּא בְּחִינַת דְּבַר ה' שֶׁעַל יָדוֹ נַעֲשׂוּ שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ. בִּבְחִינַת בִּדְבַר ה' שָׁמַיִם נַעֲשׂוּ, כַּמְבֹאָר בְּדִבְרֵי רַבֵּנוּ זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר. וְזֶה בְּחִינַת אד' שְׂפָתַי תִפְתָּח שֶׁאוֹמְרִים קֹדֶם הַתְּפִלָּה, כִּי הַדִּבּוּר שֶׁל הַתְּפִלָּה הוּא דְּבַר ה' כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל. נִמְצָא שֶׁהַתְּפִלָּה הִיא בְּחִינַת חִדּוּשׁ הָעוֹלָם בְּחִינַת דְּבַר ה' וְכוּ' כַּנַּ"ל. וְעַל-כֵּן תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית רְשׁוּת. כִּי הִתְגַּלּוּת הַבְּרִיאָה הִוא בְּחִינַת אוֹר בְּחִינַת וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹקִים יְהִי אוֹר וְכוּ'. וְקֹדֶם הַבְּרִיאָה זֶה בְּחִינַת חֹשֶׁךְ. כִּי קֹדֶם הַבְּרִיאָה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַשִּיג, וְעַל-כֵּן נִקְרָא בְּחִינַת חֹשֶׁךְ מֵעֹמֶק הַמֻּשָּג. בִּבְחִינַת יוֹצֵר אוֹר וּבוֹרֵא חֹשֶׁךְ. כְּמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא בַּכַּוָּנוֹת, שֶׁיְּצִירָה נִקְרָא אוֹר וּבְרִיאָה חֹשֶׁךְ, מֵחֲמַת שֶׁבְּרִיאָה לְמַעְלָה מִיצִירָה וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַשִּיג שָׁם, עַל-כֵּן נִקְרָא חֹשֶׁךְ מֵעֹמֶק הַמֻּשָּג. בְּחִינַת יָשֶׁת חֹשֶׁךְ סִתְרוֹ. וְעַל-כֵּן גַּם בִּשְׁעַת הַבְּרִיאָה בָּרָא ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ הַחֹשֶׁךְ קֹדֶם לְהָאוֹר בְּרֵישָׁא חֲשׁוֹכָא וְהָדַר נְהוֹרָא. כִּי הַחֹשֶׁךְ שֶׁקָּדַם לְהָאוֹר מְרַמֵּז עַל קֹדֶם הַבְּרִיאָה שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת יָשֶׁת חֹשֶׁךְ סִתְרוֹ. וְאָז בִּבְחִינַת חֹשֶׁךְ בִּבְחִינַת קֹדֶם הַבְּרִיאָה דְּהַיְנוּ קֹדֶם שֶׁנֶּאֶצְלוּ נִשְׁמוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל, אָז הָיָה הָעוֹלָם בְּחִינַת אֶפְשָׁרִי הַמְצִיאוּת מֵאַחַר שֶׁעֲדַיִן לֹא נִבְרְאוּ נִשְׁמוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל. וְזֶה בְּחִינַת תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית רְשׁוּת. כִּי הַתְּפִלָּה הִיא בְּחִינַת בְּרִיאַת הָעוֹלָם. כִּי הַתְּפִלָּה יֵשׁ לָהּ שֹׁרֶשׁ לְמַעְלָה, כִּי גַּם ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ מִתְפַּלֵּל כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה מִנַּיִן שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ-בָּרוּךְ-הוּא מִתְפַּלֵּל וְכוּ'. וְאָז בְּעַרְבִית אָז הַתְּפִלָּה הִיא בְּחִינַת רְשׁוּת בְּחִינַת אֶפְשָׁרִי הַמְצִיאוּת, כִּי עֲדַיִן אֵין חוֹבָה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לִבְרֹא אֶת הָעוֹלָם מֵאַחַר שֶׁגַּם נִשְׁמוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל עֲדַיִן לֹא נִבְרְאוּ. וְעַל-כֵּן יַעֲקֹב תִּקֵּן תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית. כִּי יִשְׂרָאֵל עָלָה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֵאשִׁית בָּרָא וְכוּ' בִּשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּקְרְאוּ רֵאשִׁית וְכוּ'. נִמְצָא שֶׁרֵאשִׁית הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁל הַבְּרִיאָה הָיָה יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְאָז בִּבְחִינַת רֵאשִׁית הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה הָיָה הָעוֹלָם אֶפְשָׁרִי הַמְצִיאוּת כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, מֵאַחַר שֶׁעֲדַיִן לֹא נִבְרְאוּ נִשְׁמוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל רַק שֶׁעָלָה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה, וְהָיָה הַדָּבָר בִּרְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ. וְעַל-כֵּן אָז בִּתְחִלַּת הַבְּרִיאָה דְּהַיְנוּ כְּשֶׁעָלָה יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה אָז הָיָה הָעוֹלָם אֶפְשָׁרִי הַמְצִיאוּת כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל:

segments.he: ועל-כן יעקב תקן תפלת ערבית שהיא רשות. כי ראשית המחשבה אי אפשר להשיג והוא בחינת חשך מעמק המשג כנזכר לעיל ושם עדין העולם בבחינת אפשרי המציאות. ועל כן שם התפלה היא בבחינת רשות. כי כביכול עדין אין חובה לדבר דברי התפלה שהם בחינת בדבר ה' שמים נעשו וכו' כנזכר לעיל. כי עדין העולם הוא אפשרי המציאות בחינת רשות, כי עדין לא נבראו ישראל רק שעלה במחשבה כנזכר לעיל. ועל כן בעת שמתחיל להתגלות בחינת יעקב אז התפלה היא רשות בחינת תפלת ערבית רשות וכו' וכנזכר לעיל. אבל אחר כך שתקן יעקב תפלת ערבית ונתגלו נשמות ישראל, כי בלילה נבראים נשמות ישראל בבחינת חדשים לבקרים וכו', ועל כן באור הבקר שמתגלה אור הבריאה, כי עקר הבריאה היא בחינת אור כנזכר לעיל, על כן אז התפלה היא בחינת חובה. כי אז כשכבר נתגלו נשמות ישראל היה ה' יתברך כביכול מחיב לדבר ולברא את העולם בשביל ישראל כנזכר לעיל. ועל כן אז ביום שהוא עקר הבריאה אחר שכבר יצאו נשמות ישראל, אז התפלה שהיא דבר ה' היא בחינת חובה. כי כביכול ה' יתברך מחיב לדבר בחינת תפלה שהיא בחינת דבר ה' ולברא את העולם בשביל ישראל שהכל נברא בשביל ישראל כנזכר לעיל:
segments.en:
"Why do you leap, you hunchbacked mountains? The mountain G-d desired for His dwelling — Hashem shall dwell there forever." The Sitra Achra — the idolaters and wicked who oppose holiness — arise each time to uproot everything, chas v'shalom, wanting to tear down to the very foundation: "remember, Hashem, against the children of Edom the day of Yerushalayim — who said: raze it, raze it, to its very foundation!"; "against Your people they scheme, and conspire against Your sheltered ones; they say: come, let us destroy them as a nation, and the name of Israel shall be remembered no more." This is true for every person at all times: "the wicked watches the righteous and seeks to kill him"; "every day a man's evil inclination renews against him and seeks to kill him" — "but Hashem will not abandon him to his hand."

For we already have a strong foundation — we are the children of Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yaakov; we already received the holy Torah; we are strong in our holy emunah and boast in it: "fortunate are we — how good is our portion!" — arising and retiring, unifying His Name twice daily. Therefore every Jew must revive himself through the foundation of emunah within him — the essential foundation upon which everything stands: "Chavakuk came and established them on one — the holy emunah": "the righteous shall live by his emunah."

Therefore one must remember the Exodus daily — we then saw His G-dliness revealed, eye to eye, through all the awesome signs and wonders: "remember His wonders that He performed." In every generation, great tzadikim come and establish foundations that can never be demolished: "a tzadik is the foundation of the world." This is the foundation of the Bais HaMikdash, for which David labored his entire life until he found its Place and foundation: "remember, Hashem, for David... who swore to Hashem... if I give sleep to my eyes... until I find a place for Hashem." The essential thing is the foundation of holiness — the Place and foundation of the Bais HaMikdash that David found (= Mashiach). Upon this foundation the Bais HaMikdash was built twice. Though through our many sins the Sitra Achra overpowered and destroyed the Bais HaMikdash twice — their effort was in vain, for the foundation can never be destroyed: "this is My resting place forever; here I shall dwell, for I have desired it."

Though it is certainly a great, bitter suffering that the Bais HaMikdash was destroyed (and one must mourn and lament at midnight every night), one cannot lament all day — one must console oneself, as established in Tikun Chatzos and the kinos, concluding with words of comfort. Through sadness and lament alone, life is impossible — the essential vitality is joy.

Therefore, one who wishes to work on his eternal end must cry out each day (especially at midnight) over his sins that delay the Bais HaMikdash's rebuilding — the essential crying being over the obstruction and prevention of joy: "the joy of our hearts has ceased." One must cry and pray until Hashem has mercy, consoling us from our hearts' sadness, gladdening us with His salvation — through what we already merited: receiving the Torah, drawing close to true tzadikim, all the points of Torah and mitzvos we already merited through His kindness and great wonders. The essential thing: the foundation of emunah (= the foundation of the Bais HaMikdash that David found = Mashiach) — this can never be destroyed.

They destroyed only the building above the foundation — the aspect of the roof [gag]. The entire building relative to the foundation is the aspect of the roof. "What ails you that you went up entirely to the rooftops?" — the verse says: what do you boast about? — "you went up entirely to the rooftops": the entire destruction is only the rooftops — the building above the foundation. But the building's foundation (= the essential building) can never be destroyed.

"Why do you leap, you hunchbacked mountains?" — gavnunim [hunchbacked] = gav [back] = roof and upper story. David tells the destroyers: why do you leap and dance, you hunchbacked mountains? All your might is only over the gavnunim — you destroyed the back and roof (= the building above the foundation). But the very foundation of holiness — the foundation of the Bais HaMikdash — you can never destroy: "the mountain G-d desired for His dwelling — Hashem shall dwell there forever." The foundation of the Bais HaMikdash that David Mashiach found — this will remain forever, until it is rebuilt speedily in our days as an eternal structure never to be destroyed.

This is: "when you build a new house" — alluding to the Third Bais HaMikdash, when a new light will shine upon Tziyon: "behold, I am doing a new thing; now it shall spring forth." The Third Bais HaMikdash is therefore called a "new house." "You shall make a railing for your roof, that the one who falls shall not fall from it" — each person must now engage in building the future new house. The essential thing: to make a railing for the roof so the building above the foundation is built and fortified well, never to be destroyed again, chas v'shalom. "You shall not place blood in your house, for the one who falls shall fall" — all transgressions are the aspect of "blood" (coming through the intensifying of blood in the 365 sinews corresponding to the 365 negative commandments). Through this the fallen have fallen, Rachmana litzlan, and through this the Bais HaMikdash was destroyed. Therefore one must repair the building: "make a railing for your roof" — building the new house with such tikunim that no more "blood" will be placed in it, no more sinning, no more falling — everyone strengthening themselves to stand firm in their emunah, so the House will endure forever.

§ 69 — The Length of Exile: Hashem Awaits an Eternal Building

This is why the exile is so long — Hashem awaits an eternal building, a complete ge'ulah with no exile after it. This requires the true tzadikim of each generation to make such tikunim that Israel will never again fall from their holiness, never relapse: "I shall remove the heart of stone from your flesh... I shall cause you to walk in My statutes." Therefore it is impossible to fathom the wondrous end — for one with free will it is extremely difficult to help. Yet "Hashem's counsel shall stand forever." In His mercy He consoles and gladdens us through the holy foundations we already merited — the Exodus, the Torah, through which every Jew snatches many mitzvos daily. David already found the place of the Bais HaMikdash; it was already built twice; they offered ketores and sacrifices; they clarified all the halachos of the Torah in the Lishkas HaGazis. Through all this, the tzadikim established strong foundations for us forever — even in our destruction, these holy foundations cannot be demolished.

After the destruction, our G-d did not abandon us. Awesome, great tzadikim arose in every generation — for no generation is an orphan — even now in our generations there were awesome tzadikim who established foundations that can never be demolished: "though I have scattered them among the nations and dispersed them through the lands, I shall be for them a miniature Mikdash" — "these are the synagogues and study halls." Through this we anticipate and await the building of the new House that will never be destroyed.
segments.he_nikud: וְעַל-כֵּן יַעֲקֹב תִּקֵּן תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית שֶׁהִיא רְשׁוּת. כִּי רֵאשִׁית הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַשִּיג וְהִוא בְּחִינַת חֹשֶׁךְ מֵעֹמֶק הַמֻּשָּג כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל וְשָׁם עֲדַיִן הָעוֹלָם בִּבְחִינַת אֶפְשָׁרִי הַמְצִיאוּת. וְעַל-כֵּן שָׁם הַתְּפִלָּה הִיא בִּבְחִינַת רְשׁוּת. כִּי כִּבְיָכוֹל עֲדַיִן אֵין חוֹבָה לְדַבֵּר דִּבְרֵי הַתְּפִלָּה שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת בִּדְבַר ה' שָׁמַיִם נַעֲשׂוּ וְכוּ' כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל. כִּי עֲדַיִן הָעוֹלָם הוּא אֶפְשָׁרִי הַמְצִיאוּת בְּחִינַת רְשׁוּת, כִּי עֲדַיִן לֹא נִבְרְאוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל רַק שֶׁעָלָה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל. וְעַל-כֵּן בְּעֵת שֶׁמַּתְחִיל לְהִתְגַּלּוֹת בְּחִינַת יַעֲקֹב אָז הַתְּפִלָּה הִיא רְשׁוּת בְּחִינַת תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית רְשׁוּת וְכוּ' וְכַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל. אֲבָל אַחַר כָּךְ שֶׁתִּקֵּן יַעֲקֹב תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית וְנִתְגַּלּוּ נִשְׁמוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל, כִּי בַּלַּיְלָה נִבְרָאִים נִשְׁמוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּבְחִינַת חֲדָשִׁים לַבְּקָרִים וְכוּ', וְעַל-כֵּן בְּאוֹר הַבֹּקֶר שֶׁמִּתְגַּלֶּה אוֹר הַבְּרִיאָה, כִּי עִקַּר הַבְּרִיאָה הִיא בְּחִינַת אוֹר כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, עַל-כֵּן אָז הַתְּפִלָּה הִיא בְּחִינַת חוֹבָה. כִּי אָז כְּשֶׁכְּבָר נִתְגַּלּוּ נִשְׁמוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיָה ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ כִּבְיָכוֹל מְחֻיָּב לְדַבֵּר וְלִבְרֹא אֶת הָעוֹלָם בִּשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל. וְעַל-כֵּן אָז בַּיּוֹם שֶׁהוּא עִקַּר הַבְּרִיאָה אַחַר שֶׁכְּבָר יָצְאוּ נִשְׁמוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל, אָז הַתְּפִלָּה שֶׁהִיא דְּבַר ה' הִיא בְּחִינַת חוֹבָה. כִּי כִּבְיָכוֹל ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ מְחֻיָּב לַדָּבָר בְּחִינַת תְּפִלָּה שֶׁהִיא בְּחִינַת דְּבַר ה' וְלִבְרֹא אֶת הָעוֹלָם בִּשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהַכֹּל נִבְרָא בִּשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל:

segments.he: ועל-כן אין להאמות שהם ישמעאל ועשו אחיזה רק באברהם ויצחק. כי עקר אחיזתם הוא מהכפירות כידוע . כי אחיזתם מהסטרא אחרא שנקרא אל אחר כפירות. ועקר הכפירות הוא אפיקורסות הנזכרת לעיל שמהפכים דברי אלקים חיים ואומרים שחס ושלום העולם הוא מחיב המציאות. וטעות זה נמשך ונשתלשל להם מחמת שבאמת העולם הוא מחיב המציאות אחר שנבראו ישראל כנזכר לעיל. נמצא שעקר אחיזתם היא מבחינת אחר הבריאה, אחר שנבראו נשמות ישראל, שאז נעשה העולם על ידי נשמות ישראל בחינת מחיב המציאות. ועל ידי זה נמשך ונשתלשל אפיקורסית וטעות שלהם. אבל בשרש נשמות ישראל למעלה בשרשם אין להם אחיזה כלל. כי שם העולם עדין אפשרי המציאות ואין להם שום אחיזה שם. ועל כן ביעקב אין להם שום אחיזה, כי ישראל עלה במחשבה תחלה. כי גם עקר קדשת אברהם ויצחק הוא רק בחינת ישראל שהוא כלול משלשה אבות. ושם עקר כלליות קדשת השלשה אבות, כמו שכתוב כי ביצחק יקרא לך וכו' ולא בכל יצחק וכו', כי העקר הוא ישראל שעלה במחשבה תחלה. וזה בחינת וזכרתי את בריתי יעקב ואחר כך ואף את בריתי יצחק וכו' . נמצא שתחלת המחשבה היה ישראל, ואז היה העולם אפשרי המציאות בחינת תפלת ערבית רשות שהיא תפלת יעקב, ושם אין להם עדין שום אחיזה כנזכר לעיל. אבל תכף שכבר עלה ישראל במחשבה והתחילו להתגלות נשמות ישראל, נעשה תכף העולם בחינת מחיב המציאות. ואז כשנבראו אברהם ויצחק שכלם לא נבראו רק בשביל ישראל כמו שכתוב כה אמר ה' אל בית יעקב אשר פדה את אברהם כמו שאמרו רבותינו זכרונם לברכה במדרש . ואז העולם הוא בחינת מחיב המציאות כנזכר לעיל, מאחר שכבר נתגלה בחינת נשמות ישראל כנזכר לעיל. ועל כן אז ביום שהוא עקר הבריאה אז התפלה היא חובה כנזכר לעיל. וזה בחינת בהבראם-באברהם . כי בראשית ברא, בשביל ישראל שנקרא ראשית שעלה במחשבה תחלה, אז ברא ה', זה בחינת אפשרי המציאות, אבל אחר כך שכבר עלה ישראל במחשבה ונאצלו נשמות ישראל אז נאמר אלה תולדות השמים והארץ בהבראם, בהבראם דיקא. זה בחינת מחיב המציאות, כי אחר כך נעשה העולם בחינת מחיב המציאות בשביל ישראל. ואז ביום הוא תפלת אברהם ויצחק שיצאו אחר יעקב, כי ישראל עלה במחשבה תחלה. כמו שכתוב כה אמר ה' בראך יעקב וכו', עולמי עולמי מי בראך ישראל, ועל כן אז ביום שכבר נתגלו נשמות ישראל אז התפלה בבחינת חובה כנזכר לעיל. ועל כן שם יש אחיזה להאמות, כי עקר אחיזתם משם כנזכר לעיל. כי באמת עקר שלמות התפלה היא ביום דיקא. כי באמת זה עקר השלמות כשהעולם הוא בבחינת מחיב המציאות. דהינו כשה' יתברך עושה רצון ישראל ובורא ומקים כל העולם בשבילם כאלו היה מחיב בדבר. שזהו בחינת מה שנעשה העולם מחיב המציאות בשביל ישראל כנזכר לעיל. ובודאי זה עקר השלמות, ועקר כונת הבריאה היתה בשביל זה כדי שיהיה נכלל העולם אחר כך בחיוב המציאות על ידי ישראל וכנזכר לעיל במאמר הנזכר לעיל עין שם. אבל אף על פי כן עכשו יש להם אחיזה מבחינה זו דיקא, מבחינת אחר הבריאה דהינו אחר שנברא העולם בשביל נשמות ישראל שנאצלו תחלה. ואז אחר שנאצלו נשמות ישראל אז העולם בחינת מחיב המציאות כנזכר לעיל. ומשם משתלשל להם אחיזה לאפיקורסות ושטות שלהם כנזכר לעיל. כי ה' יתברך נותן להם מקום לטעות כדי שיהיה בחירה בעולם. אבל בבחינת יעקב 'ישראל שעלה במחשבה תחלה' שם אין להם שום אחיזה. כי באמת כשנאצלו נשמות ישראל במחשבה תחלה, היה העולם אפשרי המציאות וברצונו הטוב האציל נשמות ישראל ואחר כך ברא העולם בשבילם וכו' וכנזכר לעיל. ברוך ה' לעולם אמן ואמן ה' הטוב יכפר. ה' הטוב יכפר. כי הדברים נכונים מאד למי שיבינם על נכון באמת ובאמונה:
segments.en:
Therefore every person must gladden himself each day through the miracles and salvations of past, present, and future — the foundation of the Bais HaMikdash, established since the days of Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yaakov who prayed there (as our Sages say). Moshe Rabbainu stressed this Place many times: "the place Hashem shall choose." David Mashiach merited finding it through immense toil. This is the joy of the past miracles and salvations. The present miracles and salvations: the synagogues and study halls where Torah and tefilah are engaged in daily (= a miniature Mikdash). The essential joy: through the hope we hold for the Third Bais HaMikdash in the future, which will endure forever — when joy will increase beyond limit: "then our mouths will be filled with laughter."

So too each person must gladden his soul through all the good points he has already merited — especially that he was not made a gentile and was separated from those who err, etc. — and what he still merits snatching each day. And through the hope for the future: ultimately every Jew will certainly be rectified — "Hashem will not abandon His people"; "Hashem did not speak of wiping out the name of Israel" (said even of generations that served idolatry, as explained in Melachim II). All through the power of the true tzadikim in whose shelter we take refuge — through whom everything will be rectified. They are all our joy, vitality, and sustenance forever.

§ 70 — Three Redemptions, Three Transformations, Three Peaces: Past, Present, and Future

This is the aspect of the three p'duyos [redemptions], three hafuchos [transformations], and three sh'lomos [peaces]. They are the aspect of redemption and sweetening of judgments — nullifying sadness (= the severity of judgment, from which all exiles of body and soul, and all suffering, Rachmana litzlan) — drawing joy and peace (= ge'ulah, freedom, and the nullification of all suffering). Therefore they are recited on Motzaay Shabbos — so sadness and judgments (which awaken during the weekdays) do not overpower. For this reason we recite Vayitain Lecha etc. — many verses of joy, blessing, and peace — to draw the joy of Shabbos into the weekdays, nullifying the sadness that wants to take hold during the week. The three sets of three correspond to the three aspects of past, present, and future — through which one must gladden oneself, as above.

The three p'duyos begin: "He redeemed my soul in peace" — past tense: He already redeemed us by choosing us from all nations, giving us His Torah, separating us from those who err — from distress to relief countless times. The second: "the people said to Shaul: 'shall Yonasan die, who wrought this great salvation in Israel?'... the people redeemed Yonasan and he did not die" — alluding to every person's dangers and accusations, Rachmana litzlan. Hashem in His mercy sends into the hearts of the tzadikim to defend him — the kindnesses and goodnesses of the present: what Hashem bestows upon the guilty through the great power of the tzadikim who sustain the world and defend all. The third: "the redeemed of Hashem shall return and come to Tziyon with song; eternal joy upon their heads... gladness and joy shall they attain, and sorrow and sighing shall flee" — the essential hope and joy of the future, when we return to Tziyon and merit eternal joy. The essential thing: to transform all sorrow and sighing to joy.

The three hafuchos: First — "You have transformed my mourning to dance; You opened my sackcloth and girded me with joy" — all past tense: the past kindnesses — He performed miracles without number, transforming mourning to dance, from distress to relief countless times. Second — "Hashem your G-d did not wish to listen to Bil'am, and Hashem your G-d transformed the curse to a blessing" — the miracles and salvations in the present: awesome accusations arise each time from the Sitra Achra of wicked Bil'am who wants to uproot Israel, chas v'shalom. Hashem in His great mercy refuses to listen and transforms the curse to blessing — through the great power of Moshe Rabbainu (= the true tzadikim of each generation). Third — "then the maiden shall rejoice in dance... I shall transform their mourning to joy" — the joy of the future.

The three sh'lomos: First — "[He] creates the speech of the lips: peace, peace, to the far and near, says Hashem, and I have healed him" — past tense: He already prepared healing (= peace) for the far and near through the true tzadikim who prepared for us elixirs of life and precious, holy remedies in their holy books and words, which restore the soul through comforting counsel. "Taste and see that Hashem is good." Second — "a spirit clothed Amasai... 'peace to you, and peace to your helpers'" — alluding to the war against the true tzadikim in every generation (as is well known from what occurs in our generations and earlier). Hashem in His mercy sends into the hearts of many Jewish souls to look upon the truth — they come to the true tzadikim and those attached to them and say: "peace to you and peace to your helper." Third — "you shall say: thus to life! And you — peace" — alluding to the eternal life of the future, when the wondrous peace will be as explained in many verses.

"Hashem will give strength to His people; Hashem will bless His people with peace." The essential completeness of joy and blessing is peace — the vessel that holds blessing. Through peace — many Jewish souls gathering together — the light of joy increases. Through this one can receive the light of the above nine chambers, perceiving the Ain Sof light in mati v'lo mati. Due to the great intensity of this light, it can only be received through many vessels — many Jewish souls gathering together in love and peace around the true tzadikim who merit these lights (the lights of the tzachtzachos that heal and gladden all who are ill in soul, even the very gravely ill). The more gravely ill they are, the more precious the remedies needed — which only the greatest tzadik knows how to draw and heal with (as explained in the Torah "Mishra," LM I:30; see there). The essential thing is through peace: "for with joy you shall go out and in peace be led."

§ 71 — The Three Sounds of the Shofar: Past, Present, and Future

This is the aspect of the three sounds of the shofar: essentially tekiah, teruah, tekiah (our Sages had a doubt about the teruah sound, therefore they established blowing both teruah and shevarim, as explained in the Gemara). The tekiah before is a simple sound, and the tekiah after is a simple sound. These represent the good and kindness He already performed for us at the giving of the Torah — given with the sound of the shofar, a simple sound, for then the crookedness of the heart was completely straightened. They merited great freedom: "freedom from the evil inclination, from the angel of death, and from the subjugation of kingdoms." And in the future: "on that day a great shofar shall be blown, and the lost ones shall come" — a simple sound, for then: "they shall all know Me, from the least to the greatest." All suffering and sadness from the crookedness of the heart will be completely nullified.

In between, we blow the teruah — teruah and shevarim: groaning and wailing, as our Sages say. This is what man must do now, in the present, all the days of his life: overpower to transform all kinds of sadness (= groaning and wailing) to joy. Through this comes the essential teshuvah — through yishuv hada'as, which is through joy. The essential thing: through the power of the mitzvah of shofar, we merit truly awakening, implanting holy emunah in our hearts (= all our joy): "fortunate is the people that knows the teruah; Hashem, in the light of Your countenance they shall walk" — perceiving the light of the countenance, from which all holy da'as to know that Hashem is G-d: "in Your Name they shall exult all day." Until we merit seizing all the sorrow and sighing (from which all sins come) and transforming it to joy — the essential teshuvah: sins transformed to merits. This is the sound of the teruah — the essential thing.

§ 72 — The Mizmor "Hodu" Before Tefilah: Past, Present, and Future in Songs

This is the aspect of the entire mizmor "Hodu LaHashem" recited before tefilah at the beginning of Pesukay d'Zimrah — speaking of past, present, and future. "Remember His wonders that He performed"; "remember forever His covenant, the word He commanded for a thousand generations, which He made with Avraham" etc. — He gave us the Torah and brought us into Eretz Yisrael, the portion of our inheritance — all speaking of the great past miracles. Then: "sing to Hashem a new song; proclaim from day to day His salvation" — even each and every day He performs wondrous, awesome salvations for us. Then the future: "let the heavens rejoice and the earth exult, let the sea roar and its fullness... then all the trees of the forest shall sing before Hashem" — all said of the future.

In all this we must gladden ourselves at all times — especially before tefilah — and thank His Name for the miracles He already performed, what He does now at all times (expanding for us in distress, etc.), and what He will do for us for eternity through the power of the true tzadikim in whose shelter we take refuge. This entire mizmor "Hodu" was recited by David before the Ark when it entered its place (as explained in Divray HaYamim). The essential joy is when the Ark comes to its place — deriving from "blessed is the glory of Hashem from His place": the source of joy. The essential joy is the Torah — drawn from there. Likewise in all the songs and praises, most speak of past, present, and future — all to gladden our souls in the depth of our long exile of body and soul, so that we merit returning, drawing close, and clinging to Hashem — essentially through joy.

§ 73 — Ehyeh Asher Ehyeh: "With the Attribute of Mercy I Created, Conduct, and Will Renew the World"

This is what is found in Osiyos d'Rabbi Akiva (cited in Yalkut Reuveni, Parshas Shemos): "Another interpretation: Ehyeh Asher Ehyeh — with the attribute of mercy I created the world, with the attribute of mercy I conduct it, and with the attribute of mercy I will renew it. Another interpretation: with the attribute of good I created the world, with the attribute of good I conduct it, and I will renew it in the future." This is the above: "He was good, He is good, He will be good" — through which comes the essential joy and clinging to Him (= the vitality and sustenance). Ehyeh is Keser, as explained there on "I shall be with you and bless you." Keser (= the Place, the Arranger) is the source of joy — from which comes the ge'ulah from Egypt and all exiles. The passage concludes: "another interpretation: with the attribute of emunah I created the world" — for emunah is the aspect of joy, the foundation of everything.

§ 74 — The Three Redemptions at Hatavas Chalom: Joy Rectifies Dreams

Therefore these three p'duyos etc. are recited at Hatavas Chalom [the amelioration of a dream]. The essential tikun of a dream is through joy — as the Hatavas Chalom concludes: "go eat your bread with joy and drink your wine with a glad heart." As already explained (ois lamed-ches): sleep derives at its root from the wearying of the mind through the pursuit and obstructer; according to the tikun of the mind, so the sleep and the dreams. Therefore the essential tikun of a bad dream is through drawing the joy of the three comforters — through which the essential tikun of the mind comes. Therefore we recite then the three p'duyos, three hafuchos, etc. — through which joy and peace are drawn: the essential redemption from all suffering, nullified through joy.

§ 75 — Closing Note: "I Shall Rejoice in Hashem" — The Joy of Shma Yisrael

See the holy Zohar, Parshas Pinchas (daf 236b), on the verse "Shma Yisrael" etc. The passage states: "Rav Hamnuna Saba said: whoever performs this unification each day — joy is prepared for him from above, from the secret of these letters. Shin-Mem from this side, and Alef-Ches from this side, etc. And the sign: Esmach [I shall rejoice], as it is written: 'Anochi esmach baHashem' — in Hashem Himself — this is the holy unification, and it is fitting."

This is the entire point of all our words in this entire discourse: the inner essence of our words is that every Jew must rejoice in Hashem — "Anochi esmach baHashem" [I shall rejoice in Hashem] — this is the essential ge'ulah and salvation of every Jew. The essential thing: every Jew, however he is, must rejoice in what he merits — at least saying Shma Yisrael twice every day, as we boast: "fortunate are we — how good is our portion!" — arising and retiring, unifying His Name twice daily. This is all our vitality and hope in this world and the World to Come forever. Nothing will remain of man or of fleeting time except the joy of holy emunah, as explained above. The holy Zohar reveals that the letters of Esmach [I shall rejoice] are hinted in Shin-Mem of Shma and Alef-Ches of Echad — for one must rejoice greatly in meriting to unify His Name each day: "Anochi esmach baHashem."
